incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: increased error rate on canary routing for /v1/generate — threshold exceeded (8%) at 2026-03-15T16:07Z (thread_ts 2078904321)

samir: i'm grabbing logs, oncall hopping on — which rollout is this?

jess: it's the v4 model-routing canary (10% traffic). deploy-bot shows rollout id 20789abc started at 16:07 by me.

deploy-bot: Deploy 20789abc started: model-routing:v4 -> canary(10%).

maria: seeing 502s in the canary pods around 16:09-16:15. sample log:
```
ERROR model-runner-5a - 502 upstream timeout - downstream client cancelled
at net/http: upstream write timeout
```

leah-sre: quick heads up — the canary host tag changed to "release/v4" so the existing canary dashboard queries (tag=release:v3) return 0 results. observability gap = we got alerts but zero traces/dashboards for the new tag.

samir: so we're paged but missing the main telemetry. great. is the SLO burn metric including the canary?

jess: looks like the SLO service-level counter is scoped to service=main, not the model-runner-5a canary. alert fired on aggregated error-rate metric that DOES include the canary, but SLO dashboards don't.

prod-support: CS update: initial triage shows ~12 customers reported 502s (mostly short-lived), ticket ENG-3456 created. No revenue-impacting customers flagged yet.

maria: can we flip the canary traffic flag? rollback seems heavier. kill-switch would route canary traffic back to v3.

samir: agreed. do the kill, then confirm metrics. runbook suggests feature-flag flip when canary causes user-visible errors.

jess: run this in ops shell:
```
# flip canary routing for model-routing v4
/flipper kill model-routing v4 --scope=canary
# or via console: Feature Flags -> model-routing -> disable v4
```

maria: executing now.

incident-bot: Action logged: feature-flag flip requested by maria at 2026-03-15T16:18Z

maria: flipped the flag. traffic falling back to v3, error rate trending down in the next 2 mins.

leah-sre: confirming traces are still missing for v4 because the tracing agent wasn't tagging new canary pods — missing env var TREACE_TAG=release/v4. ops infra will need a remedy.

samir: note for postmortem: two separate observability gaps — (1) dashboard queries/filtering didn't handle the new tag format, (2) traces/ingest for canary were misconfigured so we couldn't inspect spans. both caused confusion during paging.

jess: i'm opening a postmortem ticket now with action items: fix tag mapping on dashboards, add a gating check for new tag formats on rollouts, make alert rules include SLO-scoped counters OR page different team. assigning owners.

prod-support: CS confirms errors dropped to baseline after kill. impacted customers reduced to 8 confirmed users; CS set severity to low.

maria: leaving notes for next oncall: runbook step 3 needs explicit flag flip command and the console link. i'll paste the command in the ticket.

samir: also recommend an immediate temporary change to the pager: when a canary is active, route canary-only alerts to the deployer first instead of broad oncall. avoids noisy pages when dashboards are incompatible.

jess: agreed — will add as an action.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — status: mitigated, severity: SEV-2, timeline: 16:07-16:22Z. Follow-ups: OBS-123 (dashboard tag mapping), OBS-124 (trace env var gating), RUNBOOK-57 (pager routing tweak).

maria: thanks team. handing off to tomorrow's oncall at 08:00.

samir: good job. closing thread once follow-ups are created. :thumbsup:
